deep.title: Kigali
deep.line: Capital and largest city of Rwanda

deep.text: Kigali, officially the City of Kigali also known as Kigali City, is the capital, largest city, and a province-level administrative unit of Rwanda.

deep.caption: According to oral history, the Kingdom of Rwanda was founded in the 14th century on the shores of Lake Muhazi, around 40 kilometres east of modern Kigali.

events.label: Despite a German ordinance written in 1905.
Kigali became the capital upon Rwandan independence in 1962.
Reforms in January 2020 transferred much of the districts’ power to the city-wide council.

deep.text: The earliest inhabitants of what is now Rwanda were the Twa, a group of aboriginal pygmy hunter-gatherers who settled the area between 8000 and 3000 BC and remain in the country today.
Kigali is located in the centre of Rwanda, at 1°57′S 30°4′E.

The City of Kigali is a province-level administrative unit, one of five top-level subdivisions established in 2006 alongside the country’s four provinces as part of a restructuring of local government.
The city has an average elevation of 1,567 m above sea level, with the lowest areas, in the valleys, lying at around 1,300 m.
Kigali’s central business district, sometimes known by the Kinyarwanda term mu mujyi, is on Nyarugenge Hill and was the site of the original city founded by Richard Kandt in 1907.
The house that Kandt lived in is now the Kandt House Museum of Natural History.
Attracting international visitors is a priority for city authorities, including leisure tourism, conferences and exhibitions.
